name: systemd unit
description: The fundamental managed entity. Types: service (.service), socket (.socket), target (.target), device (.device), mount (.mount), automount (.automount), swap (.swap), timer (.timer), path (.path), slice (.slice), scope (.scope). Defined by unit files at /usr/lib/systemd/system/ (vendor), /etc/systemd/system/ (admin override), /run/systemd/system/ (runtime).

name: Unit file loading precedence
description: Lookup order: /etc/systemd/system/ → /run/systemd/system/ → /usr/lib/systemd/system/. First found wins; absent earlier paths fall through. Drop-in dirs (UNIT.d/) layered on top via override.conf files. systemctl edit creates /etc/systemd/system/UNIT.d/override.conf.

name: Service unit (.service)
description: Long-running process, oneshot job, or notify-style daemon. Defined by [Service] section: ExecStart=, Type=, Restart=. Most common unit type. Lives at /etc/systemd/system/<name>.service.

name: Target unit (.target)
description: Synchronization point — a named state that other units can require/be wanted by. Replaces SysV runlevels. Examples: multi-user.target (= old runlevel 3), graphical.target (= 5), default.target (symlink to current default), basic.target (early-boot ordering anchor).

name: Socket unit (.socket)
description: Listening socket(s) systemd opens before the associated service starts (socket activation). When a connection arrives, systemd starts the service and passes the FD. Companion .service usually has the same name. Defined by [Socket] section: ListenStream=, ListenDatagram=, Accept=.

name: Timer unit (.timer)
description: Cron-like scheduled trigger. Activates the same-named .service (or Unit=). OnCalendar= for wall-clock; OnBootSec= / OnUnitActiveSec= for relative. systemd's replacement for cron.

name: Mount unit (.mount)
description: Filesystem mountpoint managed by systemd. Auto-generated from /etc/fstab entries. Encoded path: e.g. /var/lib/foo → var-lib-foo.mount. Manually creatable for advanced needs (network mounts with retry).

name: Path unit (.path)
description: Activates same-named .service when a watched path changes (PathChanged=, PathExists=, PathExistsGlob=, PathModified=, DirectoryNotEmpty=). systemd's inotify-driven activation.

name: Slice unit (.slice)
description: Cgroup container for grouping units to apply shared resource control. Hierarchy: -.slice (root) → system.slice / user.slice / machine.slice. Custom slices for resource pooling (e.g. workload.slice with MemoryMax= shared by all member services).

name: Scope unit (.scope)
description: Like service but for processes systemd didn't fork. Used by user sessions (session-N.scope under user-UID.slice) and `systemd-run --scope`. Lifetime tracked via cgroup membership.

name: Unit state: active
description: Unit running normally. Subtypes: running (process alive), exited (Type=oneshot completed RemainAfterExit=yes), waiting (Type=oneshot completed), listening (socket bound).

name: Unit state: inactive
description: Unit stopped, dead. Default for never-started units.

name: Unit state: failed
description: Service exited non-zero, was killed by signal not in SuccessExitStatus=, hit start-limit (StartLimitBurst hit StartLimitIntervalSec), or condition check failed. systemctl reset-failed clears the latched failure.

name: Unit state: activating
description: Transitional — Type=notify waiting for sd_notify(READY=1), Type=oneshot ExecStart still running, Type=forking waiting for parent fork. Stuck here = misbehaving notify daemon or slow Exec.

name: Unit state: deactivating
description: Transitional — running ExecStop; if exceeds TimeoutStopSec, escalates to KillSignal then SIGKILL.

name: Unit state: reloading
description: systemctl reload triggered ExecReload= and waiting for completion.

name: Unit state: maintenance
description: Older state name (rare in modern systemd) — corresponds to manual intervention required. Most failures land in 'failed' instead.

name: Service Type=simple
description: Default. ExecStart= IS the main process. systemd considers unit started immediately after fork+exec. No fancy sync — just go.

name: Service Type=exec
description: Like simple but waits for execve() to complete (vs just fork). Catches early exec failures. Newer (v240+) recommended default for new services.

name: Service Type=forking
description: Classic Unix daemon — main process forks, parent exits, child becomes the long-running daemon. PIDFile= helps systemd track the right child. The 'old way'; prefer Type=simple/exec/notify.

name: Service Type=oneshot
description: Runs ExecStart to completion, then unit is 'inactive (dead)' (or 'active (exited)' if RemainAfterExit=yes). Used for setup scripts, mounts, one-time migrations.

name: Service Type=notify
description: Service uses sd_notify(3) to tell systemd it's READY=1. Until then, dependents wait. Best mode for graceful startup of complex daemons (PostgreSQL, nginx-with-warmup).

name: Service Type=dbus
description: Considered started when BusName= appears on the system bus. For dbus-activated daemons.

name: Service Type=idle
description: Like simple but delays exec until all jobs are dispatched. Cosmetic — keeps shell text from interleaving with boot output.

name: Restart= policy
description: When to auto-restart on exit: no (never), always, on-success, on-failure (non-zero exit / signal / watchdog), on-abnormal (signal / timeout / abort), on-watchdog, on-abort. The most-tuned directive for resilience.

name: StartLimit (restart rate limit)
description: StartLimitIntervalSec=10s + StartLimitBurst=5 — if unit starts >5 times in 10s, it goes to 'failed' permanently (until reset-failed). Prevents restart loops from masking deeper bugs.

name: Exec environment
description: Per-service env: Environment=, EnvironmentFile= (read from path), PassEnvironment= (inherit named host env vars). UnsetEnvironment= removes. systemctl show-environment / set-environment for the manager-wide global.

name: Exec stdio handling
description: StandardInput=, StandardOutput=, StandardError= each set per-fd: null, tty, journal (default), syslog (deprecated), kmsg, journal+console, file:PATH, append:PATH, socket, fd:NAME. Default journal sends to journald.

name: User= / Group= directives
description: Drop privileges to specified user/group before ExecStart. systemd creates dynamic user (DynamicUser=yes) for ephemeral identity if requested. Works with SupplementaryGroups= for additional GIDs.

name: DynamicUser=yes
description: Allocate a transient UID/GID for the service runtime. UID picked from 61184-65519 range. Useful for sandboxing without managing static users. Implies several hardening directives by default (RemoveIPC=, PrivateTmp=, NoNewPrivileges=).

name: Wants= (soft dependency)
description: Want a unit started; if it fails, current unit still proceeds. Soft dependency. Implemented via .wants/ directory — symlink to target unit.

name: Requires= (hard dependency)
description: Want a unit started; if it fails or stops, this unit is also stopped. Hard dependency. Use Wants= for resilience.

name: Requisite= (must-already-be-started)
description: Like Requires but doesn't start the dependency — fails this unit if dependency isn't already active.

name: BindsTo=
description: Like Requires but ALSO stops this unit if the dependency goes inactive (not just fails). The strictest dependency.

name: Conflicts=
description: Cannot be active at same time as listed unit. Starting one stops the other.

name: Before= / After=
description: Ordering relationship (independent of Wants/Requires). After=foo.service means 'wait for foo.service to be active before starting me'. Doesn't IMPLY a dependency — combine with Wants/Requires for full effect.

name: Condition* vs Assert*
description: ConditionX= (e.g. ConditionPathExists=) — if false, unit silently skipped (still 'active (exited)'). AssertX= — if false, unit FAILS. Assert is for catching configuration errors loudly; Condition for opportunistic activation.

name: systemd cgroup integration
description: Every service runs in its own cgroup under its slice's cgroup. systemd manages cgroup creation/deletion automatically. Resource control directives (MemoryMax=, CPUQuota=, etc.) translate to cgroup v2 control files (memory.max, cpu.max, etc.).

name: systemd cgroup slice tree
description: Top-level: -.slice. Children: system.slice (services), user.slice (per-user user-UID.slice with session-N.scope), machine.slice (containers via systemd-machined). Each unit's cgroup nested under its slice.

name: Transient unit
description: Unit created at runtime (no on-disk file). Created via `systemd-run` or systemd's D-Bus API. Used for ad-hoc execution under systemd's resource control. Does not survive systemd reload unless made persistent.

name: Drop-in directory (.d)
description: UNIT.service.d/ directory containing override.conf or per-purpose .conf files. Layered on top of base unit file — directives can extend (Environment=, list-valued) or override (scalar). systemctl edit creates this.

name: systemd unit specifier
description: %-prefixed substitution in unit files. %u = user, %i = instance (template), %h = home dir, %t = runtime dir, %T = tmp dir, %v = kernel version, %m = machine ID, %H = hostname, %p = prefix, %P = unescaped prefix, %n = full unit name, %N = unescaped, %j = final component, %J = unescaped, %s = shell, %L = log dir, %S = state dir, %C = cache dir, %E = config dir.

name: Template + instance units
description: Template unit foo@.service can be instantiated as foo@arg.service — %i = arg in unit file. Used for per-X services (getty@tty1.service, dhcpcd@eth0.service).

name: Socket activation
description: systemd opens the listening socket; on first connect, starts the service and passes the FD. Service inherits via LISTEN_FDS env var + sd_listen_fds(3). Saves boot time (services start lazily) and supports auto-restart without dropped connections.

name: sd_notify protocol
description: Service writes status messages to NOTIFY_SOCKET (env-var path). Supported messages: READY=1, RELOADING=1, STOPPING=1, STATUS=string, ERRNO=N, BUSERROR=string, MAINPID=PID, WATCHDOG=1, EXTEND_TIMEOUT_USEC=N. Type=notify makes systemd wait for READY.

name: systemd watchdog
description: WatchdogSec= sets ping interval. Service must sd_notify(WATCHDOG=1) within. Failure → Restart=on-watchdog → kill+restart. Hardware watchdog (RuntimeWatchdogSec=) reboots on systemd hang.

name: PrivateTmp=
description: Mounts a fresh private /tmp + /var/tmp namespace for the service. Other services can't see its temp files. Default for many vendor units.

name: PrivateNetwork=
description: Service runs in fresh netns with only loopback. Cuts off network entirely — perfect for batch jobs that don't need it.

name: PrivateDevices=
description: New /dev with only minimal devices (null, zero, full, urandom, tty, ptmx). Hides hardware.

name: ProtectSystem=
description: strict (RO mount of entire FS except /dev /proc /sys), full (RO of /usr /boot /efi), true (RO of /usr /boot), false (default off). Major hardening for services that don't write FS.

name: ProtectHome=
description: yes (no /home access), read-only, tmpfs (empty tmpfs at /home), false. Stops services from rummaging in user data.

name: NoNewPrivileges=
description: Sets the prctl PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS bit. setuid binaries don't gain privs in this service. Required for running unprivileged seccomp filters.

name: SystemCallFilter=
description: Per-service seccomp filter. Allowlist syntax (positive list), denylist with ~ prefix. Pre-defined groups: @system-service, @network-io, @file-system, @basic-io, @io-event, @ipc, @timer, @resources, @setuid, @raw-io, @reboot, @swap, @clock, @cpu-emulation, @debug, @keyring, @memlock, @mount, @module, @obsolete, @pkey, @privileged, @process, @sandbox.

name: CapabilityBoundingSet=
description: Cap-bounding-set for the service (whitelist style, prefix with ~ for denylist). e.g. `CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE` lets service bind <1024 but nothing else.

name: AmbientCapabilities=
description: Set ambient capabilities for the service. Capabilities preserved into permitted+effective across non-setuid execve. The mechanism for non-root services with elevated caps (e.g. CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE).

name: ReadWritePaths= / ReadOnlyPaths= / InaccessiblePaths=
description: Per-path overlays on the FS namespace. ReadWritePaths exposes specific dirs as RW under ProtectSystem=strict. InaccessiblePaths blocks specific paths. ReadOnlyPaths makes specific dirs RO.

name: MemoryMax=
description: Hard memory limit for the cgroup. Process exceeding triggers per-cgroup OOM killer. Maps to cgroup v2 memory.max. Suffixes: K/M/G/T (1024-base) or 'infinity'.

name: MemoryHigh=
description: Throttle threshold (kernel aggressively reclaims when exceeded). No OOM. Maps to memory.high.

name: CPUQuota=
description: Percentage of one CPU (e.g. 50% = half a CPU; 200% = 2 CPUs). Maps to cgroup cpu.max via period/quota math.

name: CPUWeight=
description: Relative CPU share weight under contention (1-10000, default 100). Maps to cgroup cpu.weight.

name: TasksMax=
description: Max tasks (processes/threads) in the unit's cgroup. Maps to pids.max. Hitting it causes fork() to return EAGAIN.

name: IOWeight= / IODeviceWeight=
description: Relative IO share. Maps to cgroup io.weight / io.weight per device.

name: IOReadBandwidthMax= / IOWriteBandwidthMax= / IOReadIOPSMax= / IOWriteIOPSMax=
description: Per-device IO bandwidth/IOPS ceilings. Maps to cgroup io.max.

name: PrivateMounts=
description: Service runs in fresh mount namespace (MS_PRIVATE) — its mounts don't leak to host. Default for many sandbox-aware services.

name: ProtectKernel{Tunables,Modules,Logs}=
description: yes = forbids writes to /proc/sys, /sys/kernel; module loading; reading kernel ring buffer (dmesg). Hardening for non-admin services.

name: KillMode=
description: control-group (default: SIGTERM all in cgroup, then SIGKILL after TimeoutStopSec), process (only main process), mixed (SIGTERM main, SIGKILL the cgroup), none (no kill). control-group is usually what you want for clean shutdowns.

name: KillSignal= / RestartKillSignal=
description: Signal to send on stop (default SIGTERM). RestartKillSignal for restarts. Some daemons want SIGINT or SIGQUIT for graceful (nginx wants SIGQUIT).

name: TimeoutStopSec=
description: Grace period after SIGTERM before SIGKILL escalation. Default 90s. Set higher for slow shutdowns (DB checkpointing).

name: TimeoutStartSec=
description: Max time for unit to reach 'active'. Default 90s. Longer for cold-start daemons (Java warmup, Postgres recovery).

name: OnCalendar= timer expression
description: Wall-clock schedule. Format: DOW YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. Parts can be wildcard (*) or list (1,3,5) or range (8..18) or step (*/15). Examples: hourly = *-*-* *:00:00; daily = *-*-* 00:00:00; weekly = Mon *-*-* 00:00:00; *-*-* 08..18:00:00 = every hour 8-18.

name: Persistent=yes
description: For OnCalendar= timers: if missed (system off when scheduled), run on next boot. Critical for daily backup-style timers.

name: RandomizedDelaySec=
description: Random delay 0-N before timer fires. Spreads load when many hosts have same OnCalendar=.

name: ListenStream= / ListenDatagram=
description: Socket address spec: PORT (TCP/UDP), [::]:PORT (IPv6), /path/to/socket (unix), @abstract (Linux abstract unix), vsock:CID:PORT, fd:NAME (inherited).

name: Accept=yes vs no
description: yes = systemd accept()s each connection and forks a service@N.service per conn (inetd-style). no (default) = pass listen-FD to single service which calls accept() itself (more efficient for high conn rates).

name: Journal fields
description: Each journal entry has multiple fields. Trusted (kernel-set, '_'-prefixed): _PID, _UID, _GID, _COMM, _EXE, _CMDLINE, _CAP_EFFECTIVE, _SYSTEMD_UNIT, _SYSTEMD_SLICE, _SYSTEMD_CGROUP, _SYSTEMD_INVOCATION_ID, _BOOT_ID, _MACHINE_ID, _HOSTNAME, _SELINUX_CONTEXT, _AUDIT_SESSION, _AUDIT_LOGINUID. Application fields: MESSAGE, PRIORITY, SYSLOG_*, CODE_*, ERRNO.

name: Journal priority levels
description: PRIORITY field (matches syslog severity): 0 emerg, 1 alert, 2 crit, 3 err, 4 warning, 5 notice, 6 info, 7 debug. journalctl -p N filters; -p err shows ≤3.

name: Journal cursor
description: Opaque token uniquely identifying an entry. Used to resume reads (journalctl --cursor=...). Survives rotation.

name: Journal Storage= mode
description: persistent (write to /var/log/journal/), volatile (only /run/log/journal/, lost on reboot), auto (persistent if /var/log/journal/ exists, else volatile), none (drop entries). Default 'auto'.

name: Journal rate limiting
description: RateLimitIntervalSec=30s + RateLimitBurst=10000 = each unit can log up to 10000 messages per 30s; beyond that, journald drops + logs '<unit>: Suppressed N messages from /SYSTEMD_UNIT'. Per-unit, not global.

name: Journal vacuum
description: Free old journal data: --vacuum-size=200M (max total), --vacuum-time=2weeks (delete older), --vacuum-files=20 (max archive count).

name: Core dump handling (systemd-coredump)
description: systemd installs '|/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-coredump %P %u %g %s %t %c %h' as kernel.core_pattern. On crash, kernel pipes core to systemd-coredump which compresses + stores under /var/lib/systemd/coredump/. coredumpctl(1) queries and extracts.

name: tmpfiles.d
description: systemd-tmpfiles creates/removes/cleans files+dirs at boot and periodically. Configured via /etc/tmpfiles.d/*.conf, /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/. Each line: TYPE PATH MODE UID GID AGE ARGUMENT.

name: User scope (per-user systemd)
description: Each logged-in user gets a systemd --user instance via user@UID.service (PAM session). Manages user-level services (~/.config/systemd/user/). systemctl --user. Per-user units run inside user-UID.slice.

name: Machine scope (systemd-machined)
description: Tracks running 'machines' (containers, VMs registered via sd_notify). machinectl(1) lists/inspects/shells into. The cgroup tree under machine.slice — used by systemd-nspawn, libvirt, container runtimes that integrate.

name: RuntimeDirectory=
description: Auto-create /run/<UNIT>/ at start, owned by service user, deleted at stop. Replaces hand-rolled tmpfiles for runtime-state needs (sockets, lock files). Companion: StateDirectory=, CacheDirectory=, LogsDirectory=, ConfigurationDirectory= for /var/lib, /var/cache, /var/log, /etc respectively.

name: Boot target (default.target)
description: What systemd boots into. /etc/systemd/system/default.target is a symlink (set via systemctl set-default). graphical.target → multi-user.target → basic.target → sysinit.target → local-fs.target → ... ordering chain.

name: Shutdown / poweroff / reboot targets
description: shutdown.target (Conflicts= with everything to stop services), poweroff.target / reboot.target / halt.target (all alias for shutdown.target with different final action). systemctl reboot/poweroff/halt invokes them.

name: systemd (PID 1)
description: The init/service manager. Replaces SysV init/upstart on most distros. Manages units, dependencies, sockets, cgroups, timers, mounts. D-Bus API at /run/systemd/private and the system bus.

name: systemd-journald
description: Logging daemon. Receives messages via /run/systemd/journal/socket (sd_journal_send), kmsg (kernel), audit (auditd), syslog (forwarded). Stores in binary journal at /run/log/journal/ or /var/log/journal/. Indexed for fast queries.

name: systemd-logind
description: Session/seat/user manager. Tracks logins via PAM, manages session scopes, handles inhibition (suspend/poweroff blockers), seat assignment for multi-seat hosts.

name: systemd-coredump
description: Core-dump handler invoked via kernel.core_pattern pipe. Captures + compresses + journals + indexes core dumps. coredumpctl is the query frontend.

name: systemd-tmpfiles
description: Service that creates/cleans /tmp /run /var per tmpfiles.d/ rules. Runs at boot (--create), periodically via timer (--clean), and on shutdown (--remove).

name: systemd-analyze
description: Performance + correctness inspection tool. Subcommands: time/blame (boot timing), critical-chain, plot (SVG boot timeline), dump, verify (lint unit files), security (sandboxing audit per service), cat-config, exit-status.

name: systemd-run
description: Launch transient unit (or service/scope/timer) for ad-hoc execution under systemd's resource control. Useful for one-off command with MemoryMax= / CPUQuota=, or scheduling via --on-calendar.

name: systemd D-Bus API
description: Manager + per-unit D-Bus objects on system bus (org.freedesktop.systemd1). All unit operations (Start/Stop/Reload/Restart, get state, set property) go via D-Bus. systemctl is a D-Bus client.

name: Journal binary format
description: Custom binary log format with structured fields, deduplicated values, hash chaining (Forward Secure Sealing). Compact, indexed for queries by field. Files: system.journal (root), user-UID.journal, plus archived user-UID@TIMESTAMP.journal-INDEX rotations.

name: /etc/systemd/system/<unit>
description: Admin-installed unit files. Override + augment vendor units in /usr/lib/systemd/system/.

name: /usr/lib/systemd/system/<unit>
description: Vendor-shipped unit files (package-managed). Don't edit directly — use drop-ins or copy to /etc/systemd/system/ to override.

name: /run/systemd/system/<unit>
description: Runtime-generated unit files (transient units, generators). Cleared on reboot. Higher precedence than /usr/lib/systemd/system/, lower than /etc/systemd/system/.

name: /var/log/journal/<machine-id>/
description: Persistent journal storage. Per-machine-id dir; system.journal + user-UID.journal files inside. /run/log/journal/ for volatile.

name: /var/lib/systemd/coredump/
description: Where systemd-coredump stores compressed cores. Filename: core.<COMM>.<UID>.<BOOTID>.<PID>.<TIMESTAMP>.zst.

name: /etc/tmpfiles.d/ + /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/
description: tmpfiles.d configuration dirs. systemd-tmpfiles applies rules to manage runtime files.

name: /etc/systemd/journald.conf
description: journald configuration. Drop-ins via /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/.

name: /etc/systemd/system.conf
description: Manager (PID 1) configuration: DefaultLimitNOFILE, DefaultMemoryAccounting, RuntimeWatchdogSec, etc.

name: cgroup driver
description: systemd manages cgroups via direct file ops (write to cgroup.procs, etc.) and notifies via cgroup.events for tracking. Pure-v2 mode (DefaultCPUAccounting=yes etc. require v2). docker/cri-o coordinate via the 'systemd' cgroup driver vs 'cgroupfs' driver.

name: Journal storage driver
description: Backend for journal entries. persistent (disk), volatile (tmpfs), auto, none. Compression (Compress=yes), Forward Secure Sealing (Seal=yes).

name: Timer scheduler
description: Per-timer state machine — next-elapse computation from OnCalendar/OnBootSec/OnUnitActiveSec. Persistent= bookkeeping in /var/lib/systemd/timers/.
